precepts.text: Wisdom was present when God made the world.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Paul explains the heavens: “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Verse 4 names it: “How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” You have the sky, then space, and then where the Lord dwells, paradise, the third heaven. Those unspeakable words likely go into the name, which it is not lawful to speak.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude. It is not only the sky down here; he also created paradise. Wisdom of Solomon 9 shows it was made in the beginning. Solomon says, “Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning, which is Genesis: when God made the firmament and called it heaven. That is not only the firmament down here; it is paradise, the third heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.” That is Christ; he was there. Then Solomon prays, “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what pleases God: wisdom has to come and show you.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of what is in the heavens, and that is why the temple's pattern, which Ezekiel describes next, tells us how the heavens are built.

precepts.text: The galleries of the temple round about on their three stories.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of the holy tabernacle in heaven, so the temple's layout tells us about the heavens. Ezekiel 41:16: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. Three stories, three floors. Read on and it tells you there are chambers, a chamber here and a chamber there, the way 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

It is no coincidence that the temple was built with three stories. It goes into the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. The levels of the temple match the levels of the heavens: the sky of this earth, then space, then paradise. And above them all is the Father, at the very top, like the holy of holies.

So the three stories of Ezekiel's temple help explain “caught up to the third heaven.” Paul was taken up to the top story God built, paradise, which was made in the beginning when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

precepts.text: The ark had lower, second and third stories.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Noah's ark was built the same way. “A window shalt thou make to the ark”: there is that window again, like the narrow windows of the temple. “and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof”: the door is in the side of the boat. “with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” A lower level, a second level and a third.

The ark had three levels, the same as the temple. It is basically a floating temple. God gave Noah the same pattern he gave Solomon, and both follow the way the heavens are built.

Temple, ark and heavens all show the same three stories, and that is how Paul could speak of being caught up to the third heaven. Paradise is the third story, and the Father dwells above all of it.

precepts.text: It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. What are the stories he builds in the heaven? The first layer, the second layer and the third layer: the sky of this earth, space, and paradise. Paul calls it the third heaven. Those are the stories, three different layers.

Above them is the Father, at the very top, the holy of holies. Where he is, is infinite; it is called eternity. That is why we call him the Majesty on high. He is the highest, and the Most High, the Highest, is one of the few titles Christ does not have. That title is his Father's. They are not the same person.

Read on: “and hath founded his troop in the earth”. The troop is us. “he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.” From there, back to Genesis 1:6: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters”. The waters are space, and the firmament was made in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor sphere, and vapor means water: layers of water that circle the earth and protect it from the sun. So there are levels of heaven over the earth, then space, then paradise, with levels there too. As above, so below. Paradise was created on the second day, when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

precepts.text: Paul asked three times for his infirmity removed, but the Most High said His grace was sufficient and His strength made perfect in weakness.
precepts.point: It is good to draw near to God; he puts his trust in the Lord God that he may declare all His works.

note.label: Psalm 73: God Is Good to Israel

precepts.why:
“My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.” We all go through hard times, but we come back and understand the Most High is the strength of our heart and flesh. Paul lived this: “there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.”

Paul asked three times for his infirmity to be removed, but the Most High said, “My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.” So Paul says, “Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.”

That is what it means for God to be the strength of your heart when your flesh fails. The weakness stays, and his strength is made perfect in it. Whom have we in heaven but him, and there is none upon earth we desire beside him, so “it is good for me to draw near to God”.

precepts.point: He was revealed things he was forbidden to speak. The deep things revealed to us through Paul are already profound, yet there are things on a level we cannot even comprehend that he was not allowed to utter.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul “neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.” He tells of those revelations himself: “I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord. I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” That man “was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.”

Paul was caught up to the third heaven, into paradise, and was revealed things he was forbidden to speak. The deep things revealed to us through Paul are already profound, yet there are things on a level we cannot even comprehend that he was not allowed to utter. He was given “the abundance of the revelations”, so much that “lest I should be exalted above measure” there was given him “a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me.”

precepts.point: He called himself the chief of sinners. 2 Corinthians 12:7 says a thorn in the flesh was given to him, the messenger of Satan, lest he be exalted above measure.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
For all his credentials, Paul battled just like we battle. “And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.”

The man taught in the perfect manner of the law, the Pharisee at the top of his class, was given a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan, so that he would not be exalted above measure. The zeal of his past and the revelations of his calling did not take away the battle.

points: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as ye would not. When Paul came to the Corinthians he said, in the spirit you all expected me to be in, that is not the spirit I am coming in. They would constantly accuse Paul of things that he was not doing. Because Paul is moving in the spirit of Christ. He is telling them, I am coming in the spirit of Christ. I do not know what you expected, I do not know what you are demanding, but this is how I am moving.

Lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults. So the debates are not in righteousness, they are in unrighteousness. And tumults are when the city is in an uproar, where the magistrates have to be called, the centurions and the police have to be called to calm it down.

And lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many which have sinned already. So Paul says he shall be sorrowful for those who have already been in the midst of sin. Remember, we just read some of those in 1 Corinthians chapter 6.

And have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed. Whoa. So Paul has listed numerous sins in the two chapters we have read. But the key that I want everyone to see is, and have not repented of. They did not repent of it. So there are things that we battle with, there are things that we must fix, that we must improve on. But in order for the Lord to give that assistance there must be repentance involved. Now everybody is probably like, that is a given, everybody knows that. Everybody does not know that.

Here Paul is just making mention of two specifically, the fornication and lasciviousness. But when you read 1 Corinthians chapter 6, those were with everything else. The extortion, the thefts, the reviling, they were all together and they were all unrighteousness. So some things Paul will expound on and others he keeps very short. So there were some of the Corinthians that would not repent for the transgressions that they committed.

Videos played in class: every man in the Bible who had a rise and a fall, sexual discipline was in the downfall: David and Bathsheba, Samson and Delilah, Solomon. Our great forefathers fell, but they got back up. If you cannot master your own urges, you will burn down everything you built. Another speaker: leaving porn alone is the simplest first discipline a man can master, and if you cannot do that, what harder thing will you do? Take the thirty day challenge: either you find out you have a problem you need to address, or you prove your life is better without it, with a clearer mind and more presence in your relationships.

This is for those of you that fasted and asked God to take the porn spirit away, and a week later you were back on it. Paul was given a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet him, lest he should be exalted above measure. That thorn in the flesh goes into evil concupiscence, strong sexual desire; Paul was dealing with wicked thoughts in his mind. For this thing he besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from him.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. God is not just going to take that lust away from you. If he took away every weakness inside of you, he would be making you perfect, and you would never learn how to fight. How would you be able to teach somebody else to overcome their lust if you never fought it and dealt with it yourself? Christ's mercy is enough for us: if you fall, get back up, fix it, and stop doing it. You have to keep fighting that demon and slay it. That is how you become stronger, and as you overcome it, you become able to teach other brothers how to overcome it.

My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. These things that you have within you, you got to fight them things. That is how the power of Christ is manifest. You can't keep giving in to alcoholism, to I'm depressed, to I got low self-esteem.

You are the greatest people on the face of the planet. Brothers go out and teach blacks, Hispanics, Native Indians that you are God's chosen people, while still inside of themselves they believe they are nothing. That is sickness. You got to get over that spirit. You are greater than what you think. You are stronger than the alcohol, stronger than the pornography, stronger than what you are dealing with.

Brothers leave the truth over nothing. I'm leaving because a brother dealt with me as a father would deal with his son and told me to get in the green. I'm leaving because I don't get along with the man over me. But you get along with the white man at your job; every other nation can be over you, but your own people can't tell you nothing.

points: Paul takes pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake, because he knows it is for the Lord's sake. Persecution comes with this work; you cannot avoid it. That is why a lot of Israelites choose to join no group: they stay to themselves so they can blend in among the world and hide.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: Paul is speaking of himself: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, caught up to the third heaven, caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter. Who is in the third heaven? The Father. Hold that thought for what happens to Paul at Lystra.
Paul feared he would bewail many which had sinned already and had not repented of their uncleanness and fornication. Brethren who once repented are going backwards, often because they are idle.
Paul was caught up to the third heaven, which is paradise.
The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.
